title: No wrong option true in another version
statement: Don't build a wrong option from a detail that is true in another version or retelling of the story, because it penalises the learner who reads widely.
detail: A research note for a unit on a widely retold epic surveyed the versions children meet, among them a television series, a new film and short retellings, and warned against a wrong option built from a detail one of them adds, such as the guinea pigs of one television version (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/research/g4-u1-l3-circe-and-the-lotus-eaters.md`, lines 521-524). The note labels the warning its author's opinion; the lesson plan lists it among its integrity rules, since a distractor true elsewhere punishes the child who reads widely, the opposite of what a knowledge-rich course should do (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/content/lesson-plans/g4-u1-l3.json`, line 309).
against: The same note counts one film-derived confusion as fair game: "a child who has picked up the film secondhand may attach the forgetting flower to the woman who kept Odysseus rather than to a landfall his crew made, which is a misconception worth a distractor rather than a worry" (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/research/g4-u1-l3-circe-and-the-lotus-eaters.md`, lines 495-498), a point the lesson plan repeats (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/content/lesson-plans/g4-u1-l3.json`, line 594), though the note could not verify whether the film itself moves the flower (lines 493-495). The brief offered the rule as opinion: "One more, and it is my opinion." (`othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/research/g4-u1-l3-circe-and-the-lotus-eaters.md`, line 521).
